Briefing for 19 November 2026

Short items for 19 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

New model

Google releases Gemini 4 Neon for coding and research

Google built Neon for fast end-to-end work in software, knowledge work and science, with a 1M-token context window at $3 per million input tokens. It is rolling out in the Gemini API, AI Studio and the Gemini app.

Source: Google

In the background

Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 per share

Anthropic shares are set to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19. AP puts the valuation at about $1.5 trillion, which would make it the largest IPO so far.

Source: AP News

New model

Microsoft launches seven cheaper MAI models

At Ignite, Microsoft AI introduced models for coding, cyber defense, images, voice and transcription. It says MAI Code 2 reaches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's coding quality at about 40% of the price.

Source: Microsoft AI

Everyday tool

ChatGPT for Accounting helps close the books

OpenAI's new accounting offering connects ChatGPT to tools such as QuickBooks and Xero through plugins for invoices, reconciliation and reporting. Xero adds month-end close reviews.

Source: OpenAI

Device

OpenAI models find up to 14% gains in AMD GPUs

OpenAI says its models improved power, performance and area in AMD's flagship GPU designs by up to 14 percent. It also works with Synopsys to bring them into chip design tools.

Source: OpenAI

In the background

Boltz raises $110 million for AI drug design

Six of the world's 20 largest pharma companies use the startup's molecule design platform, and usage grew 50-fold since June, Boltz says. Bessemer led the Series A.

Source: Boltz

AI agents

KPMG tests AI agents in a real company audit

In a pilot, AI agents worked alongside a human audit team on the accounts of a UK-listed company. KPMG says the agents asked better questions in places.

Source: The Irish Times
